intro: 3DS to STL converts 3D models from 3DS to STL on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to print an old 3D Studio model or one from a model library. STL is the format every slicer reads (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer): it only stores triangles, with no units or colours.

3DS is the classic 3D Studio format, still used by many model libraries and older programs. As 3DS uses the Y axis up and 3D printing uses Z, the model is turned so it stands upright in the slicer; if you do not want that, tick “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options. 3DS is read by assimp in an isolated process with no access to the rest of the server: textures and animations are not converted, only the geometry and each material's colour.

You can apply a scale, choose the original's units if the 3DS does not store them and decide what to do with the parts: keep them separate inside the STL when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The 3DS geometry reaches the STL without being simplified or repaired. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task; they are processed on our server in the European Union and deleted when they expire.
steps: Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does the STL come out rotated or on its side?
faq.a: Because 3DS and STL may use different axes. Try ticking or unticking “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.
The 3DS material colours go into the STL if the format supports them; STL stores no colours and the note says so.

faq.q: What if the model has holes?
faq.a: The STL has the same geometry as the 3DS. To close them before printing, use Repair STL.
